summary: Steel lookout built in 1937 on Nuttby Mountain near Truro, Nova Scotia; removed in November 2013. Telecommunication towers top the summit, and a 2010 wind farm is on the mountain.

facts.design: Steel tower with an enclosed wooden observation deck
facts.status_note: Removed in November 2013. The summit now carries telecommunication towers; a 45-megawatt wind farm was built on the mountain in 2010.

access.note: Wikipedia says the peak is reached by a gated road. No source says whether the gate is open to the public.

facts.agency: Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources (earlier Department of Lands and Forest)

events.note: Steel tower arrived in Truro by train in 1937. Per McRae, it was then hauled to the summit by horse-drawn wagon.
Hurricane Edna blew the top off the tower (Canada Lookouts).
Listed as Nuttby Mtn on the Nova Scotia DNR tower list last updated 18 September 2009 (Marscan).
Removed in November 2013. SaltWire says it stood 76 years before being removed.

notes_for_editor: Dates 1937 and 2013 agree across Wikipedia, SaltWire and Canada Lookouts. Most construction detail, the staffing account and the 'highest point' claim come from one local family's recollections as reported by SaltWire; the highest-point claim is McRae's, not a survey. Height 20.1 m is converted from 'approximately 66 feet in the air' and is not stated to be to the cab floor. The SaltWire article's date is not shown on the cached page. The Lands and Forest department is named in the source as 'Lands and Forest'. No licensed photo was found. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the 2009 list entry is dated before the 2013 removal, so it says nothing about the tower after 2009. The story no longer says the list 'still' included the tower. The quoted county name is kept only inside source quotes; the story describes the location as Nova Scotia.
